question.problem: Suppose $n=3-4m,$ where $m \in \mathbb{Z}.$ Construct an argument that explains why $n$ is odd.
question.worked_solution:
An integer is *odd* if it can be written as $2a + 1,$ where $a$ is an integer.

Therefore, we complete our argument as follows:

The number $n$ is *odd* since

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =3-4m \\  & =(-4m+2)+1 \\  & =2({{-2m+1}_{⏟}}_{a})+1 \\  & =2a+1,\end{aligned}
$$

where we have defined $a=\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}-2m+1},$ which is an integer.
